gloss: to become skilled; to get used to

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {手慣|てな}れていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to become skilled at; to become practiced; to get the hang of
definitions.explanation: To become proficient at something through repeated experience, so that one can do it smoothly and without difficulty.

examples.japanese: {手慣|てな}れた{手|て}つきで{料理|りょうり}を{作|つく}る。
さすがに{手慣|てな}れたもので、{作業|さぎょう}が{速|はや}い。
examples.english: As expected from someone experienced, the work is fast.

examples.japanese: {何度|なんど}も{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すうちに{手慣|てな}れてきて、{失敗|しっぱい}しなくなった。
examples.english: After repeating it many times, I got the hang of it and stopped making mistakes.

notes:
Composed of {手|て} (hand) and {慣|な}れる (to get used to). Describes the kind of proficiency that comes from hands-on practice. Most commonly encountered in the past-tense form {手慣|てな}れた as a modifier.

USAGE:
Almost always appears as {手慣|てな}れた + noun (practiced, skilled) to describe someone performing a task with smooth, experienced ease. The phrase {手慣|てな}れた{手|て}つき (practiced hand movements) is especially common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手慣|てな}れた{手|て}つき — with practiced hands, with skilled movements
- {手慣|てな}れた{様子|ようす} — in a practiced manner
- {手慣|てな}れたもの — something one is well-practiced at

FORMS:
Ichidan (る) verb. Intransitive.
- {手慣|てな}れる → {手慣|てな}れた → {手慣|てな}れて

RELATED WORDS:
- {慣|な}れる — to get used to; the base verb, broader in meaning
- {熟練|じゅくれん} — mastery, skilled expertise; more formal
- {手際|てぎわ}がいい — to be efficient, deft; focuses on the quality of execution
